messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Dedicated pool "orchidfin-prod" reporting GPU ECC errors on node gpu-node-17. Automatic drain started (reason: hardware_ecc). Thread created 1765501234.

Devon (oncall): Ack. I'm on it, looking through node status now.

Alex W: @Devon can you confirm whether tenants were moved off or if some pods are restarting?

Devon (oncall): Node marked NotReady, cordon+drain initiated. Logs show repeated ECC errors and NVML faults. Running drain now. Command used:

```bash
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

Maria S: CSM ping — Casey, did you reach out to OrchidFin? They might be seeing errors.

Casey (CSM): Just DM'd their eng lead. They reported increased 503s on inference around 14:02 and want ETA.

Jordan P: Heads up — I also see a spot interruption on gpu-node-22 in the same pool (AWS spot termination notice at 14:03). Could be two nodes affected.

Devon (oncall): Confirmed. gpu-node-22 got a termination notice, kubelet evicted pods. I'm failing over pods to remaining nodes; autoscaler trying to spin replacements but this dedicated pool has constrained reserved capacity.

Alex W: What's the current capacity for OrchidFin? Any model evictions or queued work? Could we route critical routes to hosted fallback temporarily?

Devon (oncall): Capacity down ~40% for the pool. Some pods couldn't find GPU slots. I'll enable a temporary routing rule to push OrchidFin critical traffic to hosted-small-variant. Steps:
- add routing rule in smart-routing: OrchidFin:critical -> hosted-small-variant
- set TTL 10m
- monitor 5xx and latency

Maria S: Approved. Casey, we'll message them that we're diverting critical traffic to hosted fallback to maintain availability while we replace hardware.

Casey (CSM): Sending update now. I'll include ETA once we have hardware replacement timeframe.

infra-bot: Hardware vendor ticket created: HV-8972. On-site tech scheduled 2026-03-15 09:30 PST. Replacement GPU ordered.

Devon (oncall): Mitigation in place. Note: some long-running KV cache sessions may drop — expect transient quality degradation on a small subset of requests.

Alex W: Please add a degraded flag in Redwood Console for the pool and lower the threshold for 5xx alerts to 1% to get any regressions.

Jordan P: I'll enable targeted evals on our rolling prompt set to catch quality regressions early.

Devon (oncall): Drain finished for gpu-node-17. Evicted 18 pods, 17 rescheduled, 1 pending due to strict GPU reqs. I manually scheduled the pending pod to gpu-node-19 with toleration/taint override.

Devon (oncall): Replacement instances booting now; expected ready in ~7-12 minutes.

sre-bot: Incident severity updated to P2 (customer-facing degraded). Notifying on-call rotation for next handoff in 30m. @Alex W assigned for monitoring.

Alex W: Handoff acknowledged. I'll take over and coordinate post-incident work. Devon please paste nvml/kernel logs when you have them.

Devon (oncall): nvml/kernel snippet:
```
[14:01:22] GPU 0: ECC Error count rising: 120 -> 452
[14:01:45] GPU 0: Reset attempted, pci-e link down
[14:02:10] Kernel oops: nvidia 0000:03:00.0: AER fatal error
```

Maria S: Customer impact summary: OrchidFin saw latency spikes and a subset of 503s during the incident window. No data plane isolation breach — workloads remained within their dedicated pool and logs indicate no cross-tenant leakage.

Casey (CSM): OrchidFin appreciated the fallback. They asked whether SLA covers hardware replacements — I told them we'll escalate and include SLA credit if applicable. I'll follow up in 24h with their account team.

Alex W: Next steps checklist:
1) Confirm replacement GPUs healthy and nodes pass e2e smoke tests for OrchidFin.
2) Remove degraded flag and revert routing rule after validation.
3) Run end-to-end smoke tests for critical routes.
4) Draft postmortem and update dedicated-pool runbook for parallel spot + hardware fault scenarios.

Jordan P: Recommend we evaluate adding a pre-provision buffer (N+1) for critical customers' dedicated pools to avoid capacity collapse during concurrent failures. I'll run cost/benefit analysis.

Devon (oncall): New nodes joined at 14:12, kube status Ready, pods scheduling. Health checks passing.

sre-bot: Mitigation successful, incident marked as resolved for now. Reminder: postmortem due within 72 hours. :white_check_mark:

Casey (CSM): Sending final customer message: "Mitigation complete, replacements in progress; postmortem will follow."

Alex W: Thanks everyone — I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates.
